predictions.experiment: Share of RL step-100 plain MATH-500 answers (T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) that open in the 'Okay' deliberation format.
predictions.recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl. Keep rows with sample == 0. If a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. For each kept row take the text field (empty or missing text counts as not matching). The row matches if the substring 'Okay' (case-sensitive) occurs within the first 30 characters of text. Statistic: matching rows / kept rows. Cap-hit rows are included like any other row.

predictions.experiment: Paired cap-hit rate difference at RL step 400, cued prompt minus plain prompt, MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/F_math500.jsonl (A, cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (B, plain). In each file keep only rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both A and B (set S; problems missing from either are dropped). A row is a cap hit if cap_hit is true, or if cap_hit is missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Statistic: (cap hits in A over S) / |S| minus (cap hits in B over S) / |S|.

predictions.experiment: Ratio of median generated length of finished answers, RL step 100 over base, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (A) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'); each file's finished set is taken separately (unpaired). Length = the n_new field (rows with n_new missing are dropped). Statistic: median length of A's finished rows divided by median length of B's finished rows (median of an even count = mean of the two middle values).

predictions.experiment: Per-token sharpness of RL step-100 finished answers relative to the cued base: share of step-100 plain finished answers whose mean_logprob exceeds the median mean_logprob of the cued base's finished answers, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (R, reference) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (X). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'). Drop rows whose mean_logprob field is missing, null or non-finite. Let M = median of mean_logprob over R's finished rows (even count: mean of the two middle values). Statistic: (number of X finished rows with mean_logprob strictly greater than M) / (number of X finished rows). Ties with M count as not greater. Cap-hit rows are excluded from both files.
